learn.title: Making a choice
learn.body: So far every line ran in order. An `if` statement lets a program choose. It tests a condition, a yes or no question, and runs a block of code only when the answer is yes.

learn.title: if and else
learn.body: `age >= 18` is true for 20, so the first block runs.

learn.title: The parts
learn.body: The condition goes in parentheses after `if`. The code to run goes between curly braces. An optional `else` block runs when the condition is false. Only one of the two blocks ever runs.

learn.title: Always use braces
learn.body: C lets you skip the braces for a single line, but this causes bugs when you add a second line later. Writing braces every time is a safe habit. Indent the code inside by four spaces so it is easy to read.

learn.title: Even or odd
steps: `1 == 0` is false, so the `if` block is skipped
The `else` block runs and prints odd

learn.body: `=` stores a value and `==` compares. Writing `if (x = 5)` is a classic bug that stores 5 instead of testing.

questions.prompt: `int x = 3;` `if (x > 5)` prints big, `else` prints small. What prints?
questions.explanation: 3 is not greater than 5, so the `else` block runs.

questions.prompt: How many blocks of an if and else run in one pass?
questions.explanation: If the condition is true the `if` block runs, otherwise the `else` block.

questions.prompt: The condition of an `if` goes inside \_\_.
To test equality in a condition, use \_\_.
`int n = 7;` With the even test `n % 2 == 0`, what does the program print, even or odd?
questions.explanation: 7 leaves remainder 1 after dividing by 2, so it is odd.

choices: It needs a semicolon after the `)`
questions.explanation: `=` stores 5 in `x`, and 5 counts as true, so the block always runs.

questions.prompt: Put the parts of an if and else in order.
questions.explanation: The condition and its block come first, then the else part.
